title: Anisotropic medium-range order uncovers dynamic crossovers in glass-forming liquids
authors: Kamlesh Mishra, Rajesh Ganapathy, Walter Kob
abstract: On cooling liquids towards their glass-transition temperature, the dramatic increase of their relaxation times is accompanied by changes in particle dynamics at two distinct temperatures: A high-T crossover, where particles become temporarily caged by their neighbors, and a low-T crossover, where the cage escape mechanism changes. While there is some evidence that the former is associated with a change in local particle arrangement, no structural modification has so far been detected across the low-T crossover, fueling scepticism about the relevance of structure for glassy dynamics. Here, we introduce a novel four-point correlation function which allows to determine a structural length scale characterizing cage anisotropy. Extensive molecular dynamics simulations reveal that this scale, as well as the mean structural length scale of the glass-former, extends into the medium range, i.e., significantly exceeds the particle size. Strikingly, the difference between these two scales - a measure of the degree of cage anisotropy - peaks at both crossover temperatures. We discuss how the presence of these peaks enables understanding the nature of the change in the microscopic transport mechanism at the two temperatures, thereby linking both dynamical crossovers to a single structural observable, the anisotropic medium-range order. This fundamental insight demonstrates that structure, extending well-beyond the local cage, is an essential ingredient for understanding the relaxation dynamics of deeply supercooled liquids.
summary: This work analyzes glass-forming liquids to determine if structural changes underpin dynamic crossovers near the glass transition. By introducing a novel four-point correlation function, the authors find that the degree of cage anisotropy peaks precisely at the crossover temperatures. This establishes that medium-range structural order, extending beyond local cages, is essential for understanding the complex relaxation dynamics of supercooled liquids.
main_problem: The paper investigates the structural basis for dynamic crossovers observed in glass-forming liquids at high-T and low-T crossover temperatures.
main_result: The authors show that the degree of cage anisotropy, quantified by a structural length scale difference, peaks at both crossover temperatures, linking the dynamics to anisotropic medium-range order.
method: They introduce and utilize a novel four-point correlation function and analyze the angular power spectrum ($S_ho(l, r)$) derived from molecular dynamics simulations.
model_or_system: The study uses molecular dynamics simulations on a glass-forming liquid, specifically a binary Lennard-Jones mixture, to probe particle dynamics near the glass transition.
key_observables: Structural length scale characterizing cage anisotropy, angular power spectrum $S_ho(l, r)$, and the difference between structural length scales of slow and fast particles.
important_parameters: High-T and low-T crossover temperatures ($T_o, T_X$), and the intermediate range structural length scale.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that the structural information encoded in the four-point correlation function is sufficient to characterize the underlying physics of the dynamic crossovers.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the LCS schematic, 3D density distributions for different particle groups, and the angular power spectra $S_ho(l, r)$ showing anisotropic features at intermediate length scales.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by introducing the novel correlation function, applying it to molecular dynamics simulations to calculate density fields and power spectra, and finally interpreting the temperature dependence of the resulting structural length scales to link them to the observed dynamic crossovers.
why_interesting: The focus on structural signatures (medium-range order) dictating dynamic transitions in supercooled liquids is highly relevant to understanding complex many-body dynamics, which shares conceptual links with glassy dynamics studied in quantum many-body systems.
